REWARD_MACHINE:
STATES: u0, u1
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u0
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, top_breach) -> u1
(u0, side_breach & !top_breach) -> u0
(u0, zombie_killed & !side_breach & !top_breach) -> u0
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, else) -> u1
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, top_breach, u1) -> -10.0
(u0, side_breach & !top_breach, u0) -> -0.5
(u0, zombie_killed & !side_breach & !top_breach, u0) -> 0.1
feedback: ACCEPT with minor notes. Semantic fidelity: the task 'keep zombies from walking past the left end of the field, when you can' spans all three lanes with a softening clause. The RM handles this well: top_breach traps to u1 with -10.0 (non-accepting), matching the environment's own success definition (no top breach), while side_breach stays in accepting u0 with a -0.5 penalty, matching the 'try not to / when you can' soft constraint. Leaving plant_trampled unpenalized is correct since it is not part of this task. FINAL_STATES: u0 is present, nonempty, declared in STATES, and accepting for the task (episode ends with no top breach); u1 is a proper non-accepting trap. Ordered transition coverage in u0 is complete: top_breach has priority (correctly subsuming top&side co-occurrence, which the domain explicitly allows), then side_breach & !top_breach, then kill-only, and the else self-loop covers the remaining combos (no-event steps and plant_trampled-only steps), so the irrelevant event is absorbed by a per-state else self-loop as required; u1's else self-loop keeps the sink stable with zero reward. Event semantics are respected: all four propositions are one-step events, so guards fire exactly on the step they occur and there is no repeated-fire or persistent/event confusion. Reward safety and boundedness: +0.1 per kill is the densest progress signal available from this event set and is bounded (~37 entries max, ~3.7 total), -0.5 per side breach and the one-shot -10.0 are bounded, else self-loops pay 0, so there are no exploit loops; the magnitude ordering (avoid top breach >> avoid side breach > kill bonus) is sensible, and killing a side-lane zombie nets +0.1 plus avoiding -0.5. No regressions are needed: the task is monotone failure (breaches cannot be undone), so having no back-transitions is right. Exact format: headers and (u, guard) -> u' / (u, guard, u') -> r syntax match the paper style; the explicit !top_breach conjuncts make the guards robust to unordered evaluation. Minor, non-blocking notes: (1) no explicit reward lines for (u0, else, u0) and (u1, else, u1) — assumed default 0; adding '(u1, else, u1) -> 0.0' would be tidier. (2) On a co-occurring breach+kill step the kill's +0.1 is forfeited by the priority ordering — bounded and rare, an acceptable design choice, though rewarding the kill alongside the breach penalty would be slightly more faithful. (3) Once in u1, further side breaches go unpunished; acceptable since the primary objective is already lost.
